dashboard.help_status:
**Indoor temperature** is the mean of the rooms. **Recommended supply temperature** is the supply Degree Dealer advises: as low as possible while the most demanding room still gets enough heat. **Heat demand** is the valve demand of that room. **Return above target** is the return temperature minus the utility's expected return (or your fixed target); below 0 is good. **Cooling (supply - return)** is how much the water cools down in the radiators; higher is better. The supply, return and outdoor tiles are your own sensors.

The text below the tiles explains the advice: raise, lower or keep the supply, why, and which room decided it. Degree Dealer does not change anything yet; the advice is for you or your own automation.
dashboard.help_supply_return: The graph shows the last 48 hours of the measured supply and return temperatures, the recommended supply temperature, the controller's supply reference (if chosen) and the outdoor temperature. When the recommended supply is below the measured supply, the house could manage with colder water. A low return compared with the supply means the radiators use the water well.
dashboard.help_setback:
**Night setback** is the most profitable setback in K for the next night, or 0 when no setback pays. Degree Dealer simulates how the house cools down (cooling time constant) and when it must start heating to be back at comfort temperature when the night ends (heat-up rate). The saving is the lower heat loss while the house is cooler (heat loss coefficient × degrees × hours × heat price). The cost is the return temperature tariff during the recovery, when the valves open fully.

The table shows the night, comfort and outdoor temperature, and for a profitable setback the lowest temperature, when heating starts and the net result. The list below shows every depth with saving, tariff cost and net result; a setback is only advised when the net result is at least your minimum saving. Until the house model is learnt the sensor is unknown and the text shows what is missing.
dashboard.help_model:
**Heat loss coefficient** (W/K) is how much heat the house loses per degree between inside and outside; it is learnt from the daily meter data or set by hand. **Cooling time constant** (hours) is how slowly the house cools when the heating is off; it is learnt at night while the valves are closed, and a heavy, well insulated house has a high value. **Heat-up rate** (K/h) is how fast the rooms heat up; 1 K/h is used until it is learnt. **Days learnt** counts the days with recorded data.

The table shows where the heat loss coefficient comes from, how many days were used, the base load per day (hot water and losses that do not depend on the weather) and R² (how well the days fit the model, 1 = perfect).
dashboard.help_rooms:
One section per room (Home Assistant area). The table shows the room temperature (mean of the temperature sensors, otherwise of the thermostats), the setpoint, the valve demand (smoothed), whether a window or door is open, whether the room is in use (motion within the last 30 minutes), the humidity, how long the room has been more than 0.5 K below the setpoint, its cooling time constant and heat-up rate, and whether it is used for the supply temperature.

Below the table are the room's thermostats, temperature sensors, windows/doors and motion sensors. While a window or door is open the room pauses learning and does not decide the supply temperature.
dashboard.reason_rooms_starved: A room has been cold with a fully open valve for a while.
dashboard.reason_valves_mostly_closed: All valves are mostly closed: the water is hotter than needed.
dashboard.reason_valves_partly_closed: The valves are partly closed: the water can be a little colder.
dashboard.reason_in_band: The most demanding valve is well open: the supply fits.
dashboard.reason_at_limit: The supply is at its configured limit.
dashboard.no_advice: No advice yet: a supply temperature and at least one room with valve demand are needed.
dashboard.missing_ua: heat loss coefficient (needs about a week of meter data, or set it by hand)
dashboard.missing_tau: cooling time constant (learnt at night while the valves are closed)
dashboard.setback_not_worth_it: No setback tonight: it does not pay
